title: (I) AUTOBIOGRAPHY: What a person must do to enter the religion
english_translation:
[R] {t.1} ... thus it is seemly that he, in the same way that he takes revenge and protects the land and cultivates (it) and calls to account and eats meat and drinks wine and has (5) a wife and a servant boy and makes a house and wealth and accumulates (it) for the sake of his body and pays taxes in the land and commits robbery and damage and be- haves tyrannically and (10) mercilessly, in that same way he should ask about the wis- dom and knowledge of the gods and think (about them) for the sake of his soul. And he also [thinks] (about them) and acts for the sake of things (15) hereafter ...

[V] {t.2} ... [ ... and children ?] which he has, he shall keep away from lust and coition and evil thought and evil speech and evil deeds. And he should keep his hand away from robbery, as well, and damage and (5) *tyranny and mercilessness. And *year after year he should *care for earth and water and fire and trees and plants and wild and domestic animals and he should not (10) hurt them much. For those, too, are alive through that light and good grace of the gods (= the Living soul). Just like that warrior and farmer, thus also do that body and (15) the soul [ ... ] is [ ... ] and [ ... ]

editorial_notes: Middle Persian transliteration and English translation were interleaved; separated into distinct fields. Preserved section markers {t.1}, {t.2}, column markers [R], [V], manuscript line numbers (5), (10), (15), and lacunae/bracketed gaps exactly as given. Some line breaks and hyphenation (e.g., “be- haves”, “wis- dom”) reflect OCR/PDF artifacts and were retained rather than normalized. The second MP block beginning “nhynz'd” lacked an explicit column marker in the raw OCR; it is retained as continuous original text following [V] {t.2}.
